summary:
Scotland diverges from the UK baseline in one live, visitor-relevant direction: the Hate Crime and Public Order (Scotland) Act 2021 (in force 1 April 2024) created the UK's only dedicated transgender-identity hate-crime aggravation. COPFS reported 104 charges carrying that aggravation in 2025-26 (up 21% on 86 the year before), and Police Scotland recorded 8,538 hate crimes in 2024-25 — the first full year of the Act. Anti-trans offending in Scotland is therefore named in charging as a distinct statutory category; in England and Wales, transgender identity appears in police recording as one of the five monitored strands, but no equivalent transgender charging aggravation exists. For an assaulted or harassed visitor that is the difference between a crime the prosecution system is built to identify by name and one it is not. The wider climate corroborates the law: Holyrood passed expansive gender-recognition reform by a two-thirds majority, and Scottish public opinion on LGBT equality runs consistently ahead of the UK average (British Social Attitudes).

What does not count against Scotland as local hostility: the Section 35 veto of that reform and the June 2026 Court of Session ruling voiding the Scottish Prison Service's trans custody guidance were both applications of UK-wide law and the UK Supreme Court's biological-sex definition — the same mechanisms visitors face in every British nation, already priced into the national score (0.48). They erased Scotland's attempt to rise above that baseline; they did not push it below. Scotland therefore scores above the national anchor: the charging machinery plus the most trans-accepting electorate and government in the Isles. Vs Wales (≈0.51): inclusive posture, no charging aggravation. Vs England: recording strand without a charging aggravation; vs Northern Ireland (0.42): withdrawn school guidance, stalled hate-crime inclusion.

sources.summary: Crown Office (prosecution service) statistical bulletin, Hate Crime in Scotland 2025-26: 104 charges with a transgender-identity aggravation, up 21% from 86 the previous year; the bulletin also reports 2,062 sexual-orientation aggravated charges (+20%). Direct evidence that the dedicated transgender aggravation under the 2021 Act is actively used in charging decisions.

Scottish Government official statistics, Hate crimes recorded by the police in Scotland 2024-25 — the first annual report under section 15 of the Hate Crime and Public Order (Scotland) Act 2021: 8,538 recorded hate crimes with breakdowns of type, victim/perpetrator characteristics and prejudice shown.

Home Office statistical release, police-recorded hate crime in England and Wales, year ending March 2025: 115,990 offences across five monitored strands, with the transgender strand down 11% on the year. Establishes the comparison baseline: England and Wales monitor transgender identity in recording but have no statutory transgender charging aggravation, unlike Scotland's 2021 Act.

localsOnly: The blocked Gender Recognition Reform Bill concerns self-declaration birth-certificate procedures for residents; the voided prison guidance determines placement of those in Scottish custody, which residents and any detained visitor share.
